title: Put the door chain on: the dangling knob in through the slide track's keyhole and along the slot to its closed end
keywords: small part on a swinging chain
insert, then slide in a narrow slot
locking up at home or in a hotel room
context: Many front doors, flats and hotel rooms have a chain door guard, which lets the door open only a few centimetres; putting it on at night is something most people have done. A guard's fitting sheet: "Mount slide plate 1/4" from edge of door at convenient height. Large hole at end of slot faces away from door jamb. Mount chain holder on door jamb so that knob on chain will reach hole in slide plate." The chain (8 links, 15 cm) hangs from its holder on the casing, a brass knob 10 mm across on its end. To put it on, the knob is caught off its swinging chain, carried up 15 cm, its 11 mm head is pushed square into the track's 14 mm keyhole on the door's face (the only place it goes in), and the knob is slid 8 cm along the 6.4 mm slot to the closed end beside the jamb, where it stays when let go. Let go early and it stays part way; pulled away from the door at the keyhole, it comes back out. One hand does it, as for a person.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the table top: x forward, y left, heights above the table. A white interior door section (35 mm thick, 20 x 45 cm, standing on the table), its face toward the robot at x 28.0, its latch edge at y -3.0, the door running to y +17.0; shut in its frame: the jamb (20 mm, 3 mm gap) and a 70 x 12 mm wooden casing from y -3.6 to -10.6, 12 mm proud of the door's face. All fixed. On the door: a brass chain guard slide track along y, 100 mm long, 18 mm tall, 6 mm proud, its middle line 30.0 cm up, closed end at y -2.4 (6 mm from the door's edge), the 14 mm keyhole centred at y +6.4; a 6.4 mm slot from the keyhole to the closed end. On the casing's middle (y -7.1): the chain holder (brass plate 22 x 45 mm); its steel chain (8 links, 152 mm, 20 g) hangs from a stud 16 mm out, 31.0 cm up, with the brass knob (9 g; body 10 mm across, 18 mm long; head 11 mm across) hanging level at its end, head toward the door, its axis 14.6 cm up. Arms at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: At the end: 1.0 when the knob's head is captured in the track (behind the lips: pulling the knob straight away from the door does not bring it out), the knob's neck within 8 mm of the slot's closed end, the knob let go (no finger within 1 cm) and still for 1 s; 0.5 when the head is captured at least 10 mm along the slot from the keyhole's centre but not at the end, or at the end still held; 0 otherwise (never put in, left in the keyhole or pulled back out). Real trial: a ruler, the trial video, then a pull test (the knob pulled straight away from the door stays in).
reset_notes: Slide the knob back to the keyhole, take it out and let it hang still from its holder, head toward the door. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The keyhole is a 14 mm square opening (real ones are round, about 14 mm). The chain is 8 rigid rods on ball joints (real links interlock); the knob hangs from it on a ball joint. The door is a fixed section of a real door, 20 cm wide by its latch edge (a whole door is about 80 cm wide); the guard, its distance from the door's edge, the jamb and the casing are true size. The door's opening against the chain is not simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper went to the hanging knob and nudged it about but never took hold of it or lifted it to the track; the left arm stayed near its start); demo: 1.0
